_comment: The conversation evaluation set. Each entry is a sequence of turns in one
conversation, and what each turn must produce.
Two different kinds of assertion live here, and they are deliberately
* 'criteria' / 'absent' assert what the MERGE carried. A subset check, so a
case states what it is about rather than every field the catalog has.
* 'carried' / 'not_carried' assert what the reply DISCLOSED. A field the
customer restated is current, not remembered, and reporting it as
remembered is a small lie they cannot check.
* 'reply_contains' asserts the disclosure reached the words a salesperson
reads, not just a JSON field.
No total is transcribed anywhere. Where a total matters, the harness
compares a fresh turn against the same request run standalone through
eval/cases.json — a number written down here would be a guess that happens

conversations.name: refine the quantity
conversations.proves: the most common second sentence a customer says is understood
conversations.note: The bare number 50 has no unit word, so the general quantity parser cannot see it. In a refinement it can only be the quantity.

conversations.name: a new subject does not inherit
conversations.proves: the failure mode the scope cut was protecting against

turns.request: letter-size flyers, one side, colour, under 250 a pack, 20 packs

conversations.note: A stated product kind and size is the customer naming a new subject. None of the flyer constraints survive, and the reply says nothing about earlier turns.

conversations.name: a weight correction corrects
conversations.proves: a weight adjusts a thing; it does not name a new one
conversations.note: This catalog has no 100 gsm A4 copy paper, so the turn is a no_match — which is the honest answer, and the point: the size and quantity were kept, only the weight changed. The reply names the carried quantity because a carried quantity changes the total.

conversations.name: a budget refinement
conversations.proves: a budget is a refinement, and a budget figure is not a quantity
conversations.note: '130' is a budget, not a quantity. Reading it as the quantity would quote 130 reams — a wrong total, not a cosmetic slip.

conversations.name: a refusal is a turn
conversations.proves: the next sentence after a refusal is usually a continuation
conversations.note: A refused turn is remembered, because the customer's next sentence is usually 'then what else have you got'. Here they name a new subject instead, so nothing is carried — including the ivory shade, which must not survive.

conversations.name: a no_match is a turn
conversations.proves: the next sentence after a no-match is a relaxation of it
conversations.note: The request that failed is exactly what the relaxation needs to see. Still a no_match — the catalog has no 300 gsm card under 200 a pack — and that is the honest answer.

conversations.name: a correction of a correction
conversations.proves: an explicit quantity wins every time, and the turn index advances
conversations.note: Two corrections in a row. The first restated a unit-bearing quantity, the second a bare one; both must land, and neither may be reported as remembered.

conversations.name: an unusable refinement asks
conversations.proves: a merged request that cannot be priced asks rather than quoting
conversations.note: The bare number is a quantity the merge must read, and 500,000 is out of range. Validation refuses it, so nothing is priced and the harness records an error rather than a quote. The alternative — quoting 20 because the refinement was unusable — would answer a question the customer did not ask.

conversations.name: a quantity-only first turn is continued
conversations.proves: a first turn whose only requirement is commercial is still a basis (BUG.md A12)
conversations.note: A quantity does not filter the catalog, so has_any_constraint() is False for turn 1. Gating the earlier criteria on that predicate discarded the conversation, and turn 2 asked again from nothing.

conversations.name: a budget-only first turn is continued
conversations.proves: a budget stated first survives into the turn that fixes the subject
conversations.note: The budget is carried and the reply says so, because carrying a budget silently is the constraint most likely to be a one-off. The same defect as case 9 from the other side: a budget is commercial-only too.

conversations.name: a turn that understood nothing does not forget
conversations.proves: an unparseable turn is answered fresh but does not erase the conversation (BUG.md A13)
conversations.note: Turn 2 states nothing, so it is answered from an empty request rather than by re-answering turn 1 — D3, and the whole point of it. But the earlier requirements must survive it, or one unparseable sentence ends the conversation: turn 3 has to still know it was A4 80gsm copy paper. Both halves are asserted, and either one alone would miss the defect.

conversations.name: a bare number that is also a grammage restates the quantity
conversations.proves: the reported sequence: 100 is a quantity in a refinement even though it is also a catalog weight (BUG.md A17)

turns.request: PaperLane Card A4 160gsm Assorted Pastels, 10 reams

conversations.note: The rule interpreter reads a lone 100 as 100 gsm, which is right in a fresh request ("A5 gloss 130") and wrong in a refinement, where the number is the quantity. Interpretation sees one turn (D1), so the merge has to undo the reading. Without it, turn 2 changed the paper as well as the quantity, and the bogus weight then survived every later turn — so returning to a quantity that had already quoted came back as no-match. Turn 3 proves the weight was carried rather than replaced.
